intended_object: The degree-zero Shapiro isomorphism H⁰(G, Coind_U^G A) ≅ H⁰(U, A), given by evaluating at 1. Here Coind_U^G A is the module of locally constant functions f : G → A with f(u g) = u·f(g), and G acts on it by right translation. The object is identified from the docstring and the module documentation (NSW 1.6.4, Ribes–Zalesskii 6.10.5).
explanation:
The definition sends a G-invariant f to f(1). Its inverse sends a U-invariant a to the constant function at a. Both directions are standard. A G-invariant element satisfies f(x) = (x•f)(1) = f(1), so it is constant. The value f(1) is U-invariant because u·f(1) = f(u) = f(1). In the other direction, the constant function at a U-invariant a is locally constant, satisfies the coinduction condition, and is G-invariant. Addition is pointwise, so the map is additive.

On generality: the only hypotheses are a group G with a topology and continuous multiplication, any subgroup U, and any additive group A with a U-action. This is at least as general as the textbook setting (profinite G, closed U, discrete A). ContinuousMul is needed so that right translates of locally constant functions stay locally constant, which makes the G-action well defined.

Mathlib has a Shapiro isomorphism only for abstract (non-topological) group cohomology of `Rep`. It has nothing for continuous cohomology with locally constant coinduced modules, so there is no Mathlib counterpart to cite.
